summary: The operator saw the landing copy live and called the screen 'very very very plain', asking for elegance — shading, colour, life, 'like we're actually changing the world'. Commit ff5c37e restyles both the email and code steps. A new Frame component gives each step a frosted, elevated, rounded card sitting on the warm paper field, with two soft drifting colour glows behind it — an accent-green glow and a warm-amber glow, both heavily blurred and low-opacity, for organic colour without clutter. The headline is now a serif display face; the primary button is a green gradient with a colour-tinted shadow; inputs gained rounded corners and a soft focus ring; a gradient hairline divider separates the story from the action; a small accent-dot wordmark sits at the top; and the card rises in gently on mount. The Tailwind theme gained a serif family (system serif stack, zero network cost — New York on iOS, Georgia elsewhere) and rise/float keyframes. All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion.

why.text: Operator: 'It showed up but it's very very very plain looking. I want it all spruced up to look elegant. Add some shading add some color. Add some life and make it look like we're actually changing the world.' The restyle deliberately stayed inside the existing paper/ink/accent palette rather than introducing a new theme — depth and warmth come from glows, elevation, gradient, and a serif face, not from new brand colours, so the login screen still belongs to the same app as the wallet behind it. Tasteful over gaudy: the wallet's tone is serious and trustworthy.

outcome.notes: [P-001] Both login steps restyled into the elegant Frame shell (commit ff5c37e). [P-002] Tailwind theme gained a serif family and rise/float motion. [P-003] all four gates green. Build-verified; NOT Carpenter-pixel-verified — no headless browser used, the operator verifies visually on the live deploy. [FEEDBACK->Foreman]: a headless-screenshot capability in the Carpenter sandbox would let visual changes be self-verified instead of leaning on the operator's phone loop.

uncertainty: This is a visual change verified only by typecheck/lint/test/build — none of which can see pixels. Tailwind silently drops unknown classes rather than erroring, and aesthetic judgement (glow strength, headline size, paragraph length on a narrow phone) cannot be gate-checked. The operator's eyes on the live deploy are the real verification, and taste may want the glows softer, the headline bigger, or the paragraph shorter.
next: Operator looks at the restyled screen on the live deploy and redirects the visual direction if wanted. Operator decides whether ff5c37e goes to main so the live Netlify deploy picks it up. If the look lands, the same Frame treatment could be extended to the passphrase, unlock, and identity-ceremony screens for consistency.
